body:
**Early career and firm**
- Started in 1990 as a floor trader with Kotak Securities in Mumbai. Joined Parag Parikh Securities in 1994 as research analyst and fund manager, and returned to Kochi in 1999 — [Wikipedia, citing The Hindu BusinessLine 28 Jul 2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porinju_Veliyath)
- Founded Equity Intelligence India Pvt Ltd in Kochi in 2002 as a value-investing fund manager. He is also a director of Arya Vaidya Pharmacy — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porinju_Veliyath)
- A weak secondary profile says he once held about 8% of Geojit Securities (unverified) — [Steemit profile](https://steemit.com/porinjuveliyath/@niveza-india/the-smart-investor-porinju-veliyath). In 2025–26 news, Equity Intelligence was reported acquiring a 1.43% stake in Geojit Financial Services — [ScanX](https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/orders-deals/porinju-v-veliyath-s-equity-intelligence-acquires-1-43-stake-in-geojit-financial-services/29821118)
- Kerala links: Veliyath held about 5% of Kerala Ayurveda at end-March 2025. That stock rose 20% intraday to ₹511.70 in June 2025 — [Business Standard, Jun 2025](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/porinju-veliyath-portfolio-stock-zooms-20-on-huge-volumes-do-you-own-125062300478_1.html). I found no source showing Cochin Shipyard as a Porinju pick; its 2024 upper circuits were tied to orders, not to him — [Business Today, Nov 2024](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/company-stock/story/cochin-shipyard-shares-stuck-in-upper-circuit-heres-why-454949-2024-11-25)
- Other reported picks: Archies (4 lakh shares, Apr 2017), Shalimar Paints (1 lakh shares, Apr 2017), Inditrade and Ginni Filaments (Jun 2017) — [ET via Wikipedia references](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/porinju-veliyaths-firm-buys-4-lakh-shares-in-archies-shares-surge/articleshow/58121412.cms). Kaya hit an upper circuit in Jul 2024 after a Marico tie-up; it was described as "Porinju-backed" — [Business Today, Jul 2024](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/company-stock/story/porinju-veliyath-backed-kaya-shares-hit-upper-circuit-heres-why-435783-2024-07-04)
- Media nickname: ET Now called him the "SMALLCAP CZAR of India" — [ET Now on X](https://x.com/ETNOWlive/status/1857727266815353124). I found no source for the "Smallcap Shankar" label.

body:
- **All stores are leased** `[UDRHP p.140]`. DMart, by contrast, owns most stores (memdb `case_study:false-alarm-dmart-permanent-high-pe`).
- Lease liabilities ₹1,988 cr (current ₹581 cr + non-current ₹1,407 cr) `[AR26 n.33]`. **This is the whole of screener's "Borrowings: ₹1,988 cr". Bank debt is zero** (HSIE: total debt nil since FY24).
- Total lease cash outflow FY26 ₹689 cr (5.3% of sales). P&L lease cost under Ind AS 116 is ₹716 cr (ROU amortisation 479 + interest 170 + short-term rent 67).
- Lease maturity: <1 year ₹621 cr, 1–5 years ₹1,618 cr, >5 years **only ₹211 cr**. These are short contracts, which gives flexibility to exit bad stores but means frequent re-pricing. Management says rentals are "not seeing significant pressure" and there was "no significant renegotiation" `[CC-Q3FY26]`, `[CC-Q2]`.
- **Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins:** FY22 7.5% → FY24 8.3% → FY25 9.1% → FY26 9.8% `[HSIE]`. Q2 FY27 fell to 7.7% (from 8.5%) because of operating deleverage and wages.
